title: Add themes backup module via Shopify CLI
description:
Backup tool currently captures product images but not themes. Themes are catastrophic gap for full-site recovery: Liquid templates, sections, assets/*.js/*.css, config/settings_data.json all lost on store deletion or theme corruption.

Implement themes module that backs up all themes (live + unpublished + development) via Shopify CLI shell-out. Module runs last in expectedModules pipeline, sequentially after all other modules complete.

Output: {BACKUP_DIR}/{date}/themes/{theme_id}/ with canonical Shopify directory structure (layout/, templates/, sections/, snippets/, assets/, config/, locales/). Plus themes/themes.json snapshot from shopify theme list --json. Plus themes/{id}/.meta.json with role, name, schema_version, OS2.0 flag, CLI version, backed_up_at.

CLI integration via exec.CommandContext shell out. Token passed via SHOPIFY_CLI_THEME_TOKEN + SHOPIFY_FLAG_PASSWORD env vars (never in argv, safe from ps aux). Fallback to --password flag if env vars not honored by CLI version.

Linux: auto-install via npm install -g @shopify/cli if missing. macOS/Windows: error with manual install instructions (no sudo prompts in cron).

Per-theme errors: retry 3x exponential (2s/4s/8s), continue with other themes on failure. Module success = themes list fetched, partial theme failures recorded in status.

Docker: rework runtime stage from alpine:latest to node:20-alpine, bake @shopify/cli at build time. ~150-200MB image growth. Pinned CLI version via SHOPIFY_CLI_VERSION build arg.

Security: settings_data.json may contain third-party API keys (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, etc.). chmod 0700 on themes/ dir. README warning about sensitive backup content.

Required scopes: read_themes (add to pkg/auth/scopes.go BackupScopes).

Estimate: 19h.
design:
Architecture: backup/themes.go

ThemesModule struct {
    outputDir string
    cliPath   string
    store     string
    auth      *auth.Authenticator
}

func NewThemesModule(outputDir string, auth *auth.Authenticator, store string) *ThemesModule
func (m *ThemesModule) Run(ctx context.Context) (count int, size int64, err error)

Helpers:
- ensureCLI(ctx) (cliPath string, err error) — exec.LookPath; Linux fallback npm install -g; non-Linux returns error
- listThemes(ctx, cliPath, store, token) ([]Theme, error) — shopify theme list --json
- pullTheme(ctx, cliPath, store, token, themeID, destDir) error — shopify theme pull --theme {id} --path {dir} --no-color
- writeMeta(themeDir string, theme Theme, cliVersion string) error — themes/{id}/.meta.json
- cleanupCLIArtifacts(themeDir) error — remove .shopify/ and *.toml

Module placement: main.go:22 expectedModules append "themes" last so it runs after all other modules complete. Sequential within module — one shopify theme pull at a time to avoid saturating 40 req/sec rate limit and Node CPU.

Token env strategy:
cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
    "SHOPIFY_CLI_THEME_TOKEN=" + token,
    "SHOPIFY_FLAG_PASSWORD=" + token,
)
// No --password flag — env vars cover it
// If both env vars ignored by CLI version, fallback strategy: probe with shopify theme info --json; on auth fail re-run with --password flag

Dockerfile change:
FROM node:20-alpine AS runtime
RUN npm install -g @shopify/cli@${SHOPIFY_CLI_VERSION:-3}
COPY --from=build /app/goshopify-backup /app/
USER 65534:65534

Acceptance criteria:
1. Backup produces {date}/themes/themes.json + {date}/themes/{id}/ for every theme
2. Each theme dir contains canonical Shopify directory structure
3. No .shopify/ or shopify.theme.toml in theme dirs
4. Each theme dir has .meta.json with role/name/version/OS2.0/cli_version/backed_up_at
5. On host without shopify CLI: Linux auto-installs via npm; macOS/Windows surfaces clear error with install command
6. Theme N fails 3x → backup continues theme N+1; status.json records error
7. Module appears in status.json with status + count + fileSize
8. Tests: fake CLI via PATH manipulation, verify env var usage (not argv), verify retry, verify artifact cleanup
9. Required scopes added to pkg/auth/scopes.go BackupScopes

notes:
Resolved via interactive brainstorm (2026-05-11):

Q1 Theme scope: live + unpublished + dev (all)
Q2 CLI integration: exec.CommandContext
Q3 CLI auth: --password=$TOKEN (now via env vars to avoid ps aux leak)
Q4 Output layout: themes/{theme_id}/
Q5 Missing CLI Linux: auto-install via npm
Q5b Missing CLI non-Linux: skip auto-install, surface manual install error
Q6 Per-theme errors: continue, retry 3x
Q7 Theme list snapshot: yes themes/themes.json
Q8 Working dir: direct write into backup dir

OQ1 Docker: bake Node + CLI at build time (node:20-alpine base, ~200MB growth)
OQ2 Token leak: SHOPIFY_CLI_THEME_TOKEN + SHOPIFY_FLAG_PASSWORD env vars, fallback --password flag
OQ3 Theme metadata: yes, .meta.json per theme
OQ4 Settings secrets: backup as-is + README warning + chmod 0700
OQ5 Module order: themes last, sequential
OQ6 macOS install: skip auto-install on non-Linux
OQ7 Restore: separate beads issue

Source: context7 /shopify/cli — confirmed --password flag accepts Admin API token; SHOPIFY_FLAG_<UPPERCASE_FLAG> env var convention enforced via ESLint command-conventional-flag-env rule; SHOPIFY_CLI_THEME_TOKEN documented in Shopify Theme Access app docs.

title: Add Files API media backup module
description:
Backup tool captures product images but not Shopify Files API media: videos, generic uploads (PDFs, downloads), Model3d, alt-language images, custom blog hero images uploaded via Files API. All lost on store deletion.

Implement files module that uses GraphQL bulk query files(first: 250) to enumerate all Files API media, then downloads binaries with same concurrent downloader pattern as products images.

Module: backup/files.go
- GraphQL bulk query: files(first: 250) returns MediaImage, Video, GenericFile, Model3d types
- Download each .url field to {BACKUP_DIR}/{date}/media/{id}.{ext}
- Reuse existing image downloader concurrency pattern (IMAGE_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT = 10)
- Write files.json catalog with id, type, alt, originalSource, mimeType, fileSize

Required scope: read_files (add to pkg/auth/scopes.go BackupScopes)

Estimate: 3-4h module + 2h tests + ~1h ops = 6-7h total. Smaller than themes module since bulk query infra already exists.

Note: not blocked on themes work — independent module.

title: Add themes restore via Shopify CLI
description:
Counterpart to goshopify-backup-9bx (themes backup). Restore tool currently has no theme restore path. After themes backup module ships, restore needs to consume themes/{id}/ directories from backup tree.

Approach: shopify theme push --unpublished --path themes/{id}/ --store $STORE — creates new unpublished theme from backup contents. User then promotes to live via Shopify admin (safer than auto-publish).

Considerations:
- TUI selection: show themes from backup with role/name/id from .meta.json
- Optional --publish flag for live restore (default: unpublished, requires explicit confirmation)
- Theme ID changes on restore (new theme created) — record new ID in restore log
- Settings_data.json may need merging with current production theme to preserve in-store edits made since backup
- Rollback: track new theme ID, restore command can delete it via shopify theme delete
- Auth: reuse pkg/auth.Authenticator with RestoreScopes (write_themes scope required)
- Docker image: same node:20-alpine + @shopify/cli baked in
notes: Depends on goshopify-backup-9bx (themes backup). Separate from current restore module work because restore TUI is more complex than backup module — needs theme selection UI, conflict resolution, publish/unpublish confirmation. Estimate: 12-16h.
